name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: No red aviation codes found (19 Nov)
summary: No red aviation codes, VEI 4+ eruptions or ash-related airspace closures found as of 19 Nov; Mayon at alert level 3
state: Mayon in the Philippines was raised to alert level 3 after a moderately explosive eruption on 30 Oct; a further minor eruption on 3 Nov sent ash about 1,600 metres high and 3,903 people were displaced, with no flight disruption reported (Daily Tribune). Searches on 19 Nov found no red aviation colour code near major air routes, no VEI 4+ eruption and no major ash-related airspace closure, so the signal stays Normal.
for_you: Ongoing eruptions are local hazards. Travellers near active volcanoes should follow national observatory guidance and FCDO travel advice; airlines reroute around ash plumes when advisories are issued.
rubric_hit: Normal: no aviation colour code red and no large eruption found; Mayon at alert level 3 is a local hazard

sources.title: Daily Tribune — Mayon spews ash plume, displaces nearly 4k residents

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.
